                                         Figure 1. VLM-3R: 3D Spatial-Temporal Reasoning from Monocular Video. Unlike prior video LMMs and 3D-LLMs (a) that depend
                                         on explicit 3D inputs such as depth sensors or pre-built 3D maps, VLM-3R (b) uses an end-to-end architecture with metric-scale spatial
                                         encoders that fuse scene and camera tokens to recover implicit 3D structure directly from monocular video. This design targets spatial
                                         assistance from raw camera streams and supports detailed reasoning about spatial context, instance layout, and temporal dynamics, leading
                                         to consistently stronger performance on VSI-Bench and the proposed VSTemporalI-Bench (c).

Figure 3. Network Architecture. VLM-3R takes monocular video and language instructions as input. A vision encoder and metric-
scale geometry encoder extract frame-level appearance, camera-view pose, and globally aligned 3D structure. Spatial-Visual-View Fusion
applies 2D-3D attention and a layer projector to inject spatial tokens and view tokens into the VLM. At inference time, the model uses
these fused representations to support reliable spatial and temporal reasoning from monocular video, without requiring depth sensors or
pre-built 3D maps.

(Finetuned) are further trained using our 200K spatial reasoning QA pairs. VLM-3R ranks first among open-source VLMs, demonstrating
the effectiveness of its reconstructive instruction tuning. Within the combined open-source block, dark gray marks the best score and
light gray marks the second best. Tied Avg values share the same rank.

3D Reconstructive Instructional Tuning relies on large-scale           data The generated scene_metadata.json and

Models (LMMs), enabling them to perform tasks related to               structured spatio-temporal scene graph. This representation
spatial and temporal reasoning. We explain the construction            includes precise 3D locations, sizes, and orientations of ob-
of our 3D Reconstructive datasets, which are utilized for              jects, their semantic and instance-level identities, and the
training models subsequently evaluated on VSI-Bench [77].              dynamic viewpoint of the camera across multiple frames.

source containing comprehensive training and evaluation                tions, object-camera distances) and spatiotemporal changes
